Prime Minister Narendra Modi has arrived in Chennai this morning where he will inaugurate
projects worth 13,000 crore rupees. The Prime Minister was given a warm welcome by
Tamina Ruchi Minister, C. Joseph Vijay, his cabinet colleagues and A.I.A. DMK General
Secretary and former Chief Minister Eda Padipalani Swami along with others. The Prime Minister
held a road show and, due to the venue of the event at Porur in Chennai, were reflagged
off the metro rail service from Porur to Punnamaldi. The Prime Minister travelled
along with Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, C. Joseph Vijay in the Metro Rail.
The 14.5-kilometer Metro Rail service features a unique 3.7-kilometer double-decker structure
with advanced signalling systems designed to support driverless operations.
The Prime Minister will dedicate and inaugurate railway infrastructure projects worth over
750 crore rupees, including five Amrit stations at Palani, Veldork and Torment, Ambasa Mudram
and Paramakuri and Namakal which have been redeveloped under the Amrit Bharat

New Delhi strongly condemned the repeated attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid International
Airport over the past few days, including the dastardly attack of yesterday, which have
led to loss of lives, injuries and damage to property.
In a statement, the Minister of External Affairs expressed condolences to the families
of the deceased and wished for the speedy recovery of the injured persons.
New Delhi said that repeated attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure are completely
unacceptable and must cease immediately. It added that India stands in solidarity with
the people and the government of Saudi Arabia in defence of the sovereignty and hopes that
peace and normalcy returns to the region at the earliest.
12 people were killed and 309 injured in a Houthi attack on King Khalid International
Airport in Riyadh yesterday. Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation, GACA,
said in a statement issued in the VRS today.
The victims include four Saudi citizens and eight foreigners, including two from Bangladesh
and one each from USA, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan.
Some of the injured were in critical condition while the attack also caused property damage.
Airport operations were temporarily suspended for damage assessments and safety inspections.
The Saudi-led coalition condemned the attack as a terrorist act and vowed a decisive response.
We have more from a correspondent.
Saturday's Houthi attacks on Riyadh Airport was a third attack on the Saudi capital's
airport this week.
It was also one of the deadliest strikes on Saudi Arabia in almost a decade.
No threat alert was reported to be sounded by Saudi Arabia's warning system.
Almost 260 flights to and from Riyadh were reported to be cancelled on Saturday.
The earlier attacks this week had also caused fatalities and damaged a Saudi commercial
plane on the Tamak. The Saudi-led military coalition had also reported attempted attacks
on Dhammam airport and Al-Kharj. They vowed a decisive response to these attacks on Saudi
territory. Manishivakashwani News, Dubai. US President Donald Trump said the USA may consider
joining Saudi-led strikes against the Houthis. The Supreme Court today diverted authorities

The court said metro and train services should function normally in accordance with the

It further directed that lawyers must not be obstructed from discharging the professional
duties.
As soon as he noticed the sent on a plea seeking initiation of content proceedings against authorities

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta informed the court that N-key and exit had been restricted
at only 45 of the 303 stations across the metro network on October 10.
C.J.P.'s Abhijit Deepke, Ashutosh Raka and Saurav Das, who were placed under preventive
arrest yesterday, have been released by a special Executive Magistrate, S.E.M. Court in New Delhi
today.
According to the Delhi police, all due legal procedures were followed, and the three individuals
were produced before the S.E.M. Delhi Cant this morning.
The police said that they were released upon furnishing a surety bond of Rs.50,000
rupees for maintaining peace and good behavior for a period of one year.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined
by the mantra of Jan Seva, Siddesh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues.
Guided by this vision for Seva and Su Sarshan, the government has been ceaselessly working
towards achieving the goal of a vixit Bharat by 2047.
Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives.
Today, in a special series, we bring you how the selection process for the Padma Awards
underwent extensive changes to make it more transparent and democratic.
After 2014, the selection process for the Padma Awards underwent extensive changes.
The country's highest civilian award has been made more transparent and democratic
and the nomination process has also become easier.
Now, any citizen of the country can nominate any deserving person.
People also now have the opportunity to nominate themselves.
These reforms have transformed the Padma awards from an award with a limited reach into a People's
Award.

Authorities in Nepal have issued evacuation warnings for settlements along the Boody
Ghandaki River in Gorkha district after sudden dries in water levels swept away several
houses early this morning.
According to the preliminary reports, five to seven houses in the riverbed at Jagat
have been swept away while several other houses have feared to have been washed
away downstream. No casualties have been reported so far. The cause of the sudden
rise in water levels remains unclear. However, officials suspect that a landslide
above Shuri bus and Chumnubri rural municipality may have temporarily
blocked the river with a subsequent breach of the blockage triggering the
surge. Following floods in Nepal, vigilance has been stepped up in Bihar's
